The '''Education Reform Act of 1895''' was a Solaran literacy and education reform that commissioned the development of the [[Solaran Alphabet|Sunline]] alphabet.

== Background ==

By the late nineteenth century, [[Solara]] needed a writing system that could support mass schooling, modern printing, newspapers, commerce, military bureaucracy, and parliamentary administration. The older [[Solra]] script remained prestigious but was too difficult for rapid national literacy work.

The reform answered that problem by authorizing a new practical alphabet for the [[Solaran Language]].

== Provisions ==

Source material identifies the [[Solaran Parliament]] as the commissioning authority and describes the reform as a national literacy initiative. The act created the political basis for school testing, language-office review, and eventual official adoption of Sunline.

The new alphabet was expected to be easier to learn, compatible with printing technology, distinct from other scripts, and suited to everyday communication.

== Implementation ==

Parliament's education committee oversaw the 1895-1898 testing period in the current draft structure. The [[Solaran Language Office]] is source-attested with the 1898 official standard.

After adoption, the [[Solaran Ministry of Education]] is attested by 1899 implementation guidance and the [[Solaran Academy of Linguistics]] by 1900 post-adoption study.

After three years of school testing, Sunline was officially adopted in 1898. The reform became a major landmark in [[Solaran Education]] and modern Solaran state-building.

== Legacy ==

The act helped make Solaran public life more legible and unified. It did not remove the ceremonial importance of [[Solra]], but it separated mass literacy from elite classical training.

This made Solara better able to support modern administration before the [[Avant Great War]] and the later [[Solara-Khalindar War]].
